reason: Two of the finding's load-bearing factual claims are wrong when driven, and the consequence it derives from them is wrong as well. (1) "Eleven of the twelve columns give the reader no number by any means" is false: chart() emits a full sr paragraph reading "27 Apr, 5; 4 May, 3; 11 May, 6; 18 May, 4; 25 May, 7; 1 Jun, 5; 8 Jun, 8; 15 Jun, 6; 22 Jun, 6; 29 Jun, 8; 6 Jul, 5; 13 Jul, 12 so far" — every one of the twelve is named, and that is the keyboard/AT reading of the plot. (2) "the only visible value on the plot is the live column's '12 so far'" is false: measured at 1440 the plot also paints gridline values 6 and 12 and the record tag "Best week · 8", so three magnitudes are labelled, not one. (3) The consequence — that a reader "cannot read what a good week looks like for them" — is the one thing the plot answers most explicitly. The record line IS that answer, drawn at its own height and labelled 8, and five of the eleven complete columns land exactly on a labelled reference (three at the 6 gridline, two on the record line at 8). The residual six sit between 0 and 6 on a 168px plot where one job is 14px; that is estimation, but it is not "no number". The severity is also overstated. Nothing on this chart is visibly wrong — it has a baseline, valued gridlines, a labelled record, a dated axis, a labelled live column and a complete spoken enumeration. What is proposed is an addition, so the class is refinement, not defect, and an overstated class is on its own grounds for refusal here. The residue that IS true — a fine-pointer user gets a per-week readout from the dots and not from the columns — is worth a refinement, but not by the fix as written. The fix's own numbers are right (8 Jun = 8 in the fixture) and it does not touch a constraint; it is the mechanism that fails. It claims "the existing show/place/hide model with no new code path", and that is exactly what will not work: place() anchors the tip to el.getBoundingClientRect(), and .colw measures 168px tall at every width (it is the full plot band). A tip bound to .colw is placed above or below the whole plot, i.e. up to 168px away from the bar it names — for the 3-job week of 4 May, a 42px bar, the tip floats four bar-heights above its own mark. Correct placement requires anchoring to .bar while hovering .colw, which is a new code path, not the existing one.
sharpenedFix: If pursued as a refinement, do not make .colw a button. Keep the sr paragraph as the single keyboard/AT reading of the plot — it already names all twelve weeks in one breath, which is strictly better than twelve tab stops — and add a pointer/touch-only readout: put data-tip on the .colw band with the dots' contract (`8 finishedweek commencing 8 Jun`, partial week `12 so farweek not over`), mark the wrapper aria-hidden so nothing is spoken twice, register no tabindex, and extend place() to accept an anchor element so the band raises the tip but positions it against its child .bar's box. If the seat's focusable-button form is taken instead, the wrapper must also carry an absolutely positioned ::before with insets no greater than -3px: measured at 390 the .colw box is 22x168, and the audit's target rule fails anything whose smaller dimension is under 28px.
breaks: As written (button + no expander) it fails audit.mjs targets at 390x844: .colw measures 22x168 there, under the 28px minimum, so a green gate goes red. It adds 12 focus stops to a page that has 15, inserting them between the KPI links and the 9 dots — keyboard traversal of the surface nearly doubles for facts already available in one sr sentence, and unless the wrapper is aria-hidden every week is then announced twice (once as a button name, once in the sr paragraph). Placement is the third break: the tip lands against the 168px band, not the bar. Re-measure after it lands: audit targets and contrast at all four viewports (the focus ring paints inside the plot, over gridlines and the hatched partial bar); interaction-check's "every visible interactive element has an accessible name", "nothing invisible can take focus", "focus paints a visible treatment" and both "tooltip stays inside the window" assertions at 1440 and 390; the touch pin/dismiss path, since pointerdown preventDefault on a full-height band sits directly under the page's scroll gesture on a phone; and the partial state specifically, where there is no record tag at all, so the plot's only labelled magnitudes are the two gridlines.
